counterexample.observed: The reference renders first=[2];second=[7]. The materialized renderer renders first=[2];second=[2], and the second amount binding event reports 2 rather than 7.
sequence: Compile a template whose macro binds amount from quantity and prints amount.
Set quantity to 2, invoke the macro, then set quantity to 7 and invoke it again.
Run the reference interpreter and the materializing compiler on the same document.
Compare rendered output and the compiler's binding event plan.

invariants: For every accepted document, materialized rendering is byte-for-byte identical to reference rendering.
Each macro invocation reports the binding values that are in scope at that invocation, not values from an earlier invocation.
Every emitted binding event retains the source span of the expression that produced it.
name: template-compiler
plausible_wrong_fix: Clone only the macro's top-level child nodes before expansion. This isolates direct bindings and makes the obvious repeated-use case pass, but nodes under control-flow branches remain shared, so a later nested invocation still reuses the first invocation's binding.
